prs.title: Accept agent follow-ups through native turn input delivery
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Accept agent follow-ups through native turn input delivery

## Why

`start_or_steer_turn` rejected agent messages, preventing callers from submitting follow-up work through the turn input API.

## What changed

Route `TurnInput::InterAgentCommunication` through native agent message delivery and return `TurnInputSubmission::Accepted`, without implying an immediate turn ID. These submissions request work regardless of `trigger_turn`, retain the recipient's settings, and forward turn-start options.

Wrap plaintext messages with agent context while preserving encrypted content. Reject submissions to idle recipients when the host is draining.

## Testing

Add scenario tests and snapshots covering queued-message ordering, encrypted follow-ups, preemption at reasoning boundaries, and follow-ups arriving before or after a final answer. Extend drain-gate coverage to agent submissions with parent-turn lineage.

prs.title: Add model provider discovery to the app server
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add model provider discovery to the app server

## What changed

- Add `modelProvider/list` to return OpenAI and explicitly configured providers, provider-specific settings, and the selected default provider.
- Report `canEdit` and `canChangeDefault` based on configuration requirements, layer precedence, and whether user configuration is enabled.
- Describe gateway authentication without resolving credentials, and omit endpoint URLs that are unsuitable for display.
- Document the API and update generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models.

## Testing

Add app-server tests for provider discovery, authentication modes, unsafe URL suppression, and configuration editability, plus a Python wire-format round-trip test.

prs.title: Add model provider configuration writes to the app-server
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add model provider configuration writes to the app-server

## What changed

Add `modelProvider/config/write` to create custom gateways and patch existing custom gateway, Bedrock, and GCP settings. Return the saved provider using the same safe summary as `modelProvider/list`.

Omitted fields retain their values; explicit `null` clears nullable user overrides. Apply patches through the shared configuration queue with last-write-wins semantics, enforce field editability and validation, and preserve unexposed authentication settings.

Saving leaves provider selection and authentication unchanged. Saving the provider used by `model/list` invalidates its catalog for the next access. Include documentation and generated JSON, TypeScript, and Python protocol types.

## Testing

Add coverage for gateway creation and ID allocation, patch and null semantics, configuration policy enforcement, authentication preservation, and catalog refresh after active-provider edits. Extend Python protocol tests to verify wire round trips and reject mismatched provider IDs or fields.

prs.title: Handle steers accepted during the final transcript flush
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Handle steers accepted during the final transcript flush

## Why

Input accepted while a regular turn was flushing its transcript could miss the final pending-input check and remain unprocessed when the turn completed.

## What changed

Check pending input atomically with closing steer admission. If input was accepted, resume sampling in the same turn while preserving MCP startup requirements, and complete the turn with the updated answer.

## Testing

Add a regression test that pauses the final flush, submits a steer, and verifies that the model receives it exactly once before the same turn completes with the answer to the steer.

prs.title: Preserve timestamp ties when paginating threads
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve timestamp ties when paginating threads

## Why

Timestamp-only cursors can skip threads that share the last result's timestamp, including rollout files created in the same second.

## What changed

- Include thread IDs as tie-breakers in time-sorted listing and search cursors, and use them when resuming filesystem scans and database queries.
- Share filesystem sort-key and cursor construction so continuation cursors match the listing order, including filename-based creation times.
- Preserve support for legacy timestamp-only cursors and their existing behavior of skipping ties.

## Testing

Update regression coverage for pagination through filesystem timestamp ties, legacy cursors, thread IDs in database fallback cursors, and search cursors for all time-based sort keys.

prs.title: Add a feature-gated account check for CLI thread resume
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add a feature-gated account check for CLI thread resume

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `cli_resume_account_check` feature. When enabled for `codex-tui` and `codex_exec`, reject resuming or attaching to a local thread if its recorded creator user or workspace differs from the current ChatGPT account. Return an error directing the user to sign in with the original account.

Carry creator IDs through stored thread metadata and check them before loading resume history. Preserve existing behavior for untagged threads, other clients, and authentication modes without a comparable ChatGPT account.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for account and workspace mismatches, matching accounts, legacy and paginated history, ID and path lookup, and the feature's default and bypass behavior. Verify that switching back to the original account permits attachment to a loaded thread and that creator metadata remains unchanged.

prs.title: Support model catalog overrides for plugin guidance
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support model catalog overrides for plugin guidance

## What changed

- Add `model_messages.plugins` overrides for generic usage guidance, selected-plugin hints, and recommendation introductions, with independent fallback to bundled wording for missing or invalid fields.
- Validate text limits and required template placeholders while keeping plugin identities, available capabilities, and eligibility controlled by the client.
- Track generic guidance changes across model switches and session resume, emitting replacement or retirement notices and supporting legacy snapshots and retained history.

## Testing

Add unit and scenario coverage for sparse overrides, literal text preservation, template validation, UTF-8 size bounds, capability filtering, recommendation fallback, and guidance recovery after resume.

prs.title: Add native patch support to direct Guardian review
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add native patch support to direct Guardian review

## What changed

Allow `guardian_review` to assess recorded native `apply_patch` calls alongside `exec_command` calls. Use the existing patch preparation and approval logic without applying the patch, and skip assessment when approval is unnecessary.

## Testing

Add coverage that compares direct and live patch review inputs, verifies that an allow decision leaves files unchanged, and checks that writable files skip review without writes or model requests.

prs.title: Support permission requests in direct Guardian review
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support permission requests in direct Guardian review

## What changed

Allow `guardian_review` to assess a final recorded `request_permissions` call without granting permissions. Build the review action using the same permission request preparation as live review, while continuing to reject earlier permission requests in the recorded history.

Return no assessment when the approval policy is `never` or granular policy disables permission requests.

## Testing

Add coverage comparing live and direct permission review inputs, plus tests that disallowed requests return no assessment without contacting the reviewer.

prs.title: Add a standalone HTTP MCP server for the agent message board
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add a standalone HTTP MCP server for the agent message board

## What changed

- Add `codex-message-board-mcp` to serve discussion tools at `/mcp` through ordinary MCP configuration, backed by the existing SQLite board and a read-only Codex registry.
- Require bearer authentication and validate `threadId` and `sessionId` metadata against persisted agent membership. Support additional allowed HTTP hosts with `--allowed-host`.
- Expose a reusable `serve_http` library entry point and scope retry deduplication to the caller within an MCP session.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for a child posting and its restarted parent reading the persisted board, including reads while a database writer lock is held. Cover invalid tokens, disallowed hosts, missing caller metadata, invalid membership, and startup without an existing registry.

prs.title: Package the message board MCP connection as a plugin
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Package the message board MCP connection as a plugin

## What changed

Add a `message-board` plugin with connection metadata for the HTTP MCP server. It defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp`, uses `CODEX_MESSAGE_BOARD_TOKEN` for bearer authentication, and marks the server as required.

Document installation and endpoint overrides through `mcp_servers.codex_message_board`. Installing the plugin does not start the server.

## Testing

Extend the HTTP board integration scenario to cover both direct configuration and plugin installation, verifying that a child can post a decision and its restarted parent can discover the same board and read it. Add a plugin context snapshot and include the plugin resources in Bazel test data.

prs.title: Add an in-memory launcher for the message-board MCP server
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add an in-memory launcher for the message-board MCP server

## What changed

Expose `launch_in_memory()` and `LocalServer` to run a loopback HTTP endpoint with generated bearer credentials. Runners register a shared in-memory board per session through `add_board(session_id, host)`, using `MessageBoardHost` for membership, clocks, and notifications without a SQLite registry.

The handle exposes the endpoint and authorization header for MCP configuration, including plugin endpoint overrides. Dropping it cancels HTTP and MCP sessions; `shutdown().await` also waits for completion.

## Testing

Extend the parent/child HTTP integration scenario to cover the in-memory launcher, plugin endpoint overrides, host-provided timestamps, authentication and invalid identity rejection, and operation without creating a SQLite board database.

prs.title: Scope local history discovery to the current ChatGPT account
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Scope local history discovery to the current ChatGPT account

## What changed

- Add `currentAccountOnly` to `thread/list` and `thread/search`, defaulting to `false`, and enable it for TUI history discovery, resume pickers, and task mentions.
- Mark newly created threads as account-scoped and require each recorded creator user or account ID to match the current login. Older threads and threads without creator IDs remain shared; API-key logins continue to see all local history.
- Preserve account scope through resume and revert, including fallback to original rollout metadata when an older binary drops the marker. Forks receive new-thread scope.
- Skip unreadable rollout headers in scoped discovery and filter search candidates before reading snippets. Direct access by thread ID remains available.

## Testing

Add coverage for account matching, shared legacy history, list page refilling, search pagination, API-key visibility, and scope preservation across reverts. Extend rollout lookup coverage to compressed active and archived files.

prs.title: Fix live stream reflow at the allocated conversation width
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix live stream reflow at the allocated conversation width

## Why

Streaming answers and plans need to wrap to the conversation's allocated width, which can differ from the terminal width. Resizing while reading earlier output should not report new activity unless new output has arrived.

## What changed

Reflow live streams when preparing the owned conversation layout, using its allocated width. Update the observed live revision after presentation-only reflow so it does not trigger `New activity`, while preserving notifications for unseen output.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for streaming answer and plan tables across width changes, including a narrow-layout snapshot, preservation of the reading position, and activity notifications when new output arrives before a resize.

prs.title: Support direct Guardian review of patches invoked through exec_command
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support direct Guardian review of patches invoked through exec_command

## Why

Direct Guardian review rejected recorded `exec_command` calls intercepted as `apply_patch`, even though normal execution could review those patches.

## What changed

Share intercepted patch preparation between execution and direct review so Guardian assesses the verified patch and its approval requirement without applying it.

## Testing

Extend the direct patch review scenario to cover `exec_command` heredocs alongside native `apply_patch` calls, asserting identical live and direct review inputs and no file writes after direct approval.

prs.title: Release message-board state before HTTP shutdown returns
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Release message-board state before HTTP shutdown returns

## Why

Connected legacy MCP sessions and HTTP keep-alive connections can retain message-board state after shutdown. Pending board bindings also need cancellation before they can dispatch a tool call.

## What changed

Explicitly close MCP sessions after HTTP drains and track binding factories and handlers until they release their state. Cancel pending bindings during shutdown while allowing already-dispatched board operations to finish. Clarify that `LocalServer::shutdown` waits for cleanup, while dropping the server initiates it.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for shutdown with a connected legacy client, a paused board binding, and an unauthenticated keep-alive connection. Assert that shutdown releases the board host before returning.

prs.title: Defer Guardian context trimming in elastic preparation
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Defer Guardian context trimming in elastic preparation

## What changed

- Thread `ContextBudgeting` through synchronous context and image preparation. Elastic mode preserves candidates for later entry capping and allocation; existing reviewer callers continue to use `Fixed`.
- Defer transcript selection, supporting-text caps, and image budget admission in elastic mode while preserving exact planned actions. Mark host framing as protected and distinguish optional user messages from required manual approvals.
- Add `ElasticBudgetConfig` validation requiring section minimums, including fallback policies, to sum to `DEFAULT_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS`.

## Testing

Extend tests for elastic transcript preservation, deferred native tool-call limits, oversized planned actions, image allocation, and section minimum totals above and below the required budget.

prs.title: Extract model-provider unit tests into separate files
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Extract model-provider unit tests into separate files

## What changed

Move inline tests for authentication, bearer auth, model endpoints, and providers into dedicated `*_tests.rs` files. Register workspace-routing tests under the `workspace_routing` module and keep test-only imports with the tests.

prs.title: Verify queued network approval wakeups before polling again
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Verify queued network approval wakeups before polling again

## What changed

Strengthen the execution cancellation test to verify that a session approval wakes a queued request before it is polled again. Assert that the request remains unwoken while the session policy commit lock is held, then receives a wakeup after the grant completes.

Wait for the second request to hold a prompt queue reference and install a counting waker on its semaphore. Share `WakeCount` with the existing manual prompt wakeup tests.

prs.title: Skip attribution for direct MCP tool calls
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Skip attribution for direct MCP tool calls

## Why

`CodexThread::call_mcp_tool` returns only the tool result, so computing attribution and creating a cached runtime binding for these calls is unnecessary.

## What changed

Add `McpRuntime::latest_call_tool_without_attribution` and use it for direct thread calls. Validate the call, wait for server startup, and dispatch through the latest connections without capturing an attribution binding.

## Testing

Extend the runtime binding cache test to verify that a successful call without attribution leaves the cached binding empty. Update the test server to return a successful tool result.

prs.title: Refine additional-context byte histogram buckets
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Refine additional-context byte histogram buckets

## Why

The previous histogram placed post-truncation values just over 4,000 bytes in a bucket ending at 8,000 bytes, obscuring their size near the truncation cap.

## What changed

Use logarithmic boundaries through 4 MiB for `codex.additional_context.value_bytes`, with an explicit 4 KiB boundary near the truncation cap.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that post-truncation samples between 4,024 and 4,043 bytes land in buckets ending at or below 4 KiB while preserving their sum and count.

prs.title: Retire the daemon_auto_start feature flag
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Retire the daemon_auto_start feature flag

## What changed

Eligible interactive launches now start or reuse the shared daemon regardless of `features.daemon_auto_start`. Remote-control daemon eligibility also no longer checks this flag. Use `--no-daemon` to run without the shared background server.

Treat `daemon_auto_start` as removed: ignore configured values with a migration notice, ignore managed requirements with a warning, and hide the flag from experimental feature discovery. Remove its launch telemetry tag.

## Testing

Extend retired-feature requirement coverage and add a migration-notice snapshot. Update CLI and TUI integration tests for daemon startup and explicit `--no-daemon` usage.

prs.title: Fix model selection after provider setup
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix model selection after provider setup

## Why

After provider setup, new threads could still use the models manager created for the server's startup provider, leaving their default model inconsistent with the model picker.

## What changed

- Build a models manager from the thread's configuration when its provider differs from the startup provider.
- Invalidate the model catalog after successful Amazon Bedrock setup so subsequent model listings reflect the configured provider.

## Testing

Extend Bedrock and GCP setup integration tests to verify that a new thread's model matches the refreshed model listing. The Bedrock test also checks that the thread uses `amazon-bedrock`.

prs.title: Preserve Guardian sender context for cloud deliveries with orbit IDs
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve Guardian sender context for cloud deliveries with orbit IDs

## Why

Delegation messages containing `<source_orbit_id>` fail sender provenance parsing, leaving Guardian without the sender's instructions.

## What changed

Accept an optional `<source_orbit_id>` between `<source_thread_id>` and `<input>`, rejecting values containing `<`. Continue to derive sender authority from the source thread ID.

## Testing

Update the cross-host sender context scenario and snapshot to include orbit attribution. The scenario checks that sender evidence reaches Guardian after compaction and rollback without exposing it to the receiving agent.

prs.title: Recover WebSocket transport after transient HTTP fallback
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Recover WebSocket transport after transient HTTP fallback

## Why

A transient WebSocket failure previously kept the session on HTTP for its remaining lifetime, even if WebSocket connectivity recovered.

## What changed

- Probe WebSocket connectivity in the background during HTTP fallback, allowing a subsequent request to use a ready connection without delaying HTTP requests.
- Verify recovery with a real request and bound its first-response wait to five seconds. Keep HTTP 426 responses and recovery timeouts on HTTP for the rest of the session.
- Keep retries of an HTTP request on HTTP. If a recovered connection fails before output, replay the request over HTTP without consuming its ordinary retry budget; failures after output use normal retry accounting.
- Rate-limit recovery probes and honor `Retry-After` deadlines.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for successful recovery within a turn, disconnects before and after output, full-context replay followed by incremental WebSocket requests, persistent HTTP 426 fallback, and retry deadlines.

prs.title: Support caller-owned sideband channels for realtime attachments
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support caller-owned sideband channels for realtime attachments

## What changed

Add `RealtimeSidebandTransport` and `Op::RealtimeConversationAttachStream` so callers can attach Core to an existing realtime call through bounded JSON channels without opening or reconnecting a socket.

Read events independently of outbound backpressure, enforce a 1 MiB message limit, and drain accepted input on detach or channel closure before flushing the transcript. Pending writes are never replayed.

## Testing

Add transport and Core integration tests covering delegation without a callback socket, stalled output, attachment replacement and detach, channel closure, oversized messages, and preservation of queued transcripts in history.
